Class EpisodePlan

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.server.EpisodePlan
public final class EpisodePlan extends Object
What the client asks the server to set up for the next episode.

    • mixedTurns

      public boolean mixedTurns
      Against a copy of itself: which of the two makes its move first is drawn on every tick. Two copies of one fighter trade hit for hit on the same tick, and the hit that is dealt first is the one that counts when both are a hit from the end: with the copy always first, as up to the first runs of 0.14.0, a fighter lost 12 fights of 14 on equal terms to a copy of itself, and with the fighter always first it won 16 of 23, landing as many hits as it took either way. On a server it is whichever player's click arrives first, tick by tick.

    • cornerStart

      public boolean cornerStart
      The fight begins at a corner of the arena: the opponent stands in it with the walls behind it, and the agent a few steps out from it, looking more or less its way.

    • seed

      public long seed
      The fight's chances (where the two start, every choice the bot makes) are drawn from this, so that a fight it lost can be set up again exactly, from the start; 0: drawn afresh. See LostCases.

    • startYaw

      public float startYaw
      The agent's heading at the start of a fight set up again exactly; NaN: kept as it is.

    • seedYaw

      public boolean seedYaw
      A fight of a paired evaluation (Config.evalSeed): with no startYaw, the heading it starts with is drawn from seed too, not kept from where the last fight ended. The bot is placed relative to that heading, so until 23 October two networks given the same fight met the bot somewhere else whenever they had ended the fight before looking another way (Gemini's audit).

    • usedYaw

      The heading the agent was given at the start, as the server set it; kept with a fight it lost.

    • critDrill

      public static EpisodePlan critDrill(int lesson, boolean kept)
      The opponent of a crit drill, by the lesson the drill is for (see Curriculum.DRILL_RANGE and the one after it).

      The jump: it stands where it is put and does nothing, and every four seconds it is somewhere else. Half of the time that is right in the agent's face, which is where a critical hit is the thing to make: jump, swing on the way down. The other half it is farther off, from the range a sprint hit is made at to across half the arena, and there the jump is to be left alone.

      The punish crit: it walks up close, jumps and hits on the way down, every time, and after each of those hits it keeps running at the agent. A hit made like that throws the agent up and only a little way back, so the agent comes down with the opponent still in reach; that fall is what a punish crit is made from. (Up to 0.12.3 the opponent for this stood still and hit with a plain swing. Its hit carried the agent a good two blocks away from it and nothing followed, so there was hardly ever anything in reach to punish.)

    • faceDrill

      public static EpisodePlan faceDrill()
      The opponent of the first crit drill, the crit in its face: a sparring partner that never swings and cannot be kept away. It runs straight at the agent and keeps pushing into it, and a hit moves it only a little (the caller sets how little). Nothing it does can hurt, so the agent is free to find out what a jump is for: with the opponent in its face whatever it does, a sprint hit gets it nothing a critical hit does not, and a jump made while the sword recharges has it coming down, sword back, on an opponent that is still there.
